pointers.sentence: The work is done in a suite, the docstring of `ParallelTestSuite` says, because test runner classes such as `unittest.TextTestRunner` are in practice more concerned with displaying results, and are customised more often than suites: one test runner still collects every result without knowing the tests ran in parallel (`django/test/runner.py:ParallelTestSuite`).

The test command turns `"auto"` into `get_max_test_processes`: 1 where `multiprocessing.get_start_method` is not fork, spawn or forkserver, which a comment says the runner requires; otherwise the environment variable `"DJANGO_TEST_PROCESSES"`, or the number of CPUs (`django/test/runner.py:get_max_test_processes`, `django/core/management/commands/test.py:Command.handle`).

The test command turns `"auto"` into `get_max_test_processes`: 1 where `multiprocessing.get_start_method` is not fork, spawn or forkserver, which a comment says the runner requires; otherwise the environment variable `"DJANGO_TEST_PROCESSES"`, or the number of CPUs (`django/test/runner.py:get_max_test_processes`, `django/core/management/commands/test.py:Command.handle`).
The parallel runner supports the forkserver start method (`docs/releases/6.0.txt`).
`DiscoverRunner.build_suite` ends by cutting the ordered suite when more than one process is asked for (`django/test/runner.py:DiscoverRunner.build_suite`).

`partition_suite_by_case` makes each run of consecutive tests of one class a subsuite, and the ordering keeps a class's tests together ([Finding and ordering the tests: `DiscoverRunner.build_suite`](discovery.md); `django/test/runner.py:partition_suite_by_case`).

`setup_databases` clones each test database once per process as soon as it is made, with the suffixes `"1"`, `"2"` and on; `teardown_databases` destroys the clones first (`django/test/utils.py:setup_databases`; [Test databases: `BaseDatabaseCreation`](../backends/creation.md#clones-for-parallel-test-runs)).
`ParallelTestSuite.run` does the rest, in the parent (`django/test/runner.py:ParallelTestSuite.run`):

`ParallelTestSuite.handle_event` calls the method of the parent's result that each event names, with the test at the event's index in the parent's own subsuite (`django/test/runner.py:ParallelTestSuite.handle_event`).
`multiprocessing.Pool` runs `_init_worker` once in each worker as it starts (`django/test/runner.py:_init_worker`).

Slots, the docstring says, make a worker the pool starts in place of one that exited wait for the parent to free that slot, rather than take a number with no clone; the pid's own slot comes first, a comment says, so that a replacement given a dead worker's pid never holds two (`django/test/runner.py:_claim_database_clone_slot`).
Each task runs in `_run_subsuite`, which returns the index and the events (`django/test/runner.py:_run_subsuite`); a worker free again takes the next task, on the same clone.
`RemoteTestRunner.run` makes a `RemoteTestResult` with the failfast and buffering options, runs the subsuite, and prints nothing (`django/test/runner.py:RemoteTestRunner.run`).

The result records each call, but a passing subtest's, as an event: the method's name, the index of the current test in the subsuite, and the arguments, such as a failure's exception (`django/test/runner.py:RemoteTestResult`).

`RemoteTestResult.check_picklable` pickles and unpickles each exception before recording it, and on failure prints the test, the exception and advice, and lets the error rise, ending the run (`django/test/runner.py:RemoteTestResult.check_picklable`).

A failed subtest's event carries the subtest, and so the test case, which `SimpleTestCase.__getstate__` pickles, while it runs, without its outcome and whatever cannot be pickled (`django/test/testcases.py:SimpleTestCase.__getstate__`).

A later one carries only the index of the last test run: an exception from `tearDownClass` was reported in a parallel run as an error of the class's last test, test_second, and in one process as `tearDownClass` (`django/test/runner.py:RemoteTestResult.addError`).
`SerializeMixin` makes classes that share something outside their databases, such as a file, take turns (`django/test/testcases.py:SerializeMixin`).
